I finished the review and wrote it to `.terminal_claude_agent_struct_out.json`. The verdict is **ready_with_notes**: I found 24 problems and fixed 23. The one left open is minor, and several requirements from the brief are only partly covered. No separate user message came with the task, so I built the brief checklist from the run's own stated question.

**What was wrong and is now fixed:**
- **Broken citations:** the published `paper.pdf` had been compiled without its bibliography, so all 15 in-text citations showed as "??". The rebuild in `paper/workspace` resolves all of them. BibTeX on this machine is installed as `bibtex.original`, which is what I ran.
- **False claims in the paper, each checked against the run's result files:**
  - It said the 7 confirmed indicators make up the OPEN index. They don't: OPEN is a separate six-part index, and only 3 of its parts are among the confirmed indicators.
  - The development-set row of Table 4 (0.228, LR 34.5) matches no result file. The real values are 0.246 [0.222, 0.271] and LR 365.6, which the paper's own Figure 3 already showed.
  - Life & Environment was called the weakest group at +0.042. In the home-only build it scores +0.067 and Physical Sciences is weakest (+0.025); Life & Environment is weakest only in the all-papers build.
  - The share of the breadth gap was mislabelled: 0.633 is a development-set figure, not a held-out one. Separately, "73% early contact" is really exploration (contact plus later field gains); contact alone is 77.9%.
  - The AI atlas was said to cover reinforcement learning and GANs; neither is in it.
  - Four of the seven case pairs had the wrong field group (one Physical Sciences pair was labelled CS).
  - Two cited papers were misdescribed: Weng et al. was given an "AUC 0.83" and Cheng et al. "2,000 ideas". The run's research notes say about seven times random precision and about 60,000 ideas.
  - The size-matched build was said to "control for coupling", but it still includes the off-home papers that cause the coupling.
  - The "consistency predicts growth but narrower reach" result was stated without two caveats. The growth link is almost entirely a size effect, and the reversal was not confirmed on the vocabulary-free phrase population.
  - Smaller slips: the descriptions of the indicator families, the gateway episode count (8,515 held-out, not 27,393), and mixed interval types in Table 4.
- **Other outputs:**
  - The website, interactive page, report and executive summary had the same errors where they repeated them, and now match the paper.
  - The report and executive summary counted 20 artifacts (16 completed). They now say 25 commissioned and 21 completed, which matches the report's own table.
  - The website's list of code links was missing the 9 artifacts behind the main results; they are added.
  - Several bibliography entries had wrong years or types; they are corrected against Crossref. All 31 DOIs resolve.
  - The README summary needed rewriting; the new version is in the `readme_tldr` field.
- **Additions:** the paper now also reports three results the run produced but never mentioned. The size × turnover interaction is null, the event study is null, and the all-papers-versus-home-only gap is not significant on the phrase population.

**Checks:** every edited document was rebuilt and inspected page by page. The paper is now 19 pages, with no unresolved references and no overflowing lines. Both web pages render at 390px and 1440px, and the interactive page's charts still draw.

**What a reader should still know:**
- **Title left unchanged (F24, the one unfixed item):** it still says openness "predicts" breadth. The effect is a small association (about +0.07) that adds no forecasting accuracy (+0.002). I left it because the same title appears in all six outputs, and changing it in one place would make them disagree; the body text already says "associated".
- **Frame-N confirmation is PARTIAL:** openness passed the first test on the new phrase population, but its interval includes zero under the strictest controls.
- **Brief items not fully covered:**
  - Two pre-registered checks from the unfinished closure experiment (Exp11) appear only in the report, not the paper.
  - The breadth decomposition was never repeated on the phrase population.
  - I did not re-audit the report's ten record corrections one by one; I relied on the run's own correction ledger.

I also wrote `.aii/manifest.yaml` (no files are large enough to need a keep/delete decision) and a short `README.md`. Pre-edit copies of every source I changed, plus renders and scripts, are in `final_review/scratch/`.
